reported.title: Fan toggles too often during rapid band crossings
reported.description: The hysteresis counters openHold and closeHold are reset to 0 whenever the temperature leaves the respective band (lines 83 and 91), so a temperature oscillating across the 26-30 °C band re-arms both debounce counters and lets the fan flip on and off repeatedly. With HOLD_N=4 at a 50 ms tick (lines 11, 13), each crossing only needs 200 ms of sustained reading to command a new state, so the measured run produced 4 toggles in the 5000 ms window starting at 3.50 s (limit 2). There is no minimum dwell time or toggle-rate limiter on setFan (lines 33-37, 104-115) to enforce the 2-toggles-per-5000 ms rule. D6 toggled 4 times in a 5000 ms window starting at 3.50 s (limit 2), and 5 times over the whole 10.00 s run.

judge_input.spec:
- Air temperature probe on A0 at 10 mV/°C; potting-shed vent fan on D6.
- Open the fan at 30.0 °C or above; close the fan at 26.0 °C or below.
- Fan must not change state more than 2 times in any 5000 ms window.
- If the probe is floating, or temperature reads below 5.0 °C or above 100.0 °C, force the fan ON within 600 ms and hold that safe state for the duration of the fault.
- Print `shed: <temp> C fan=ON` or `shed: <temp> C fan=OFF` every 1000 ms with one decimal place.
- Reach the commanded fan state within 500 ms of a sustained in-range band crossing.
